message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of the **Canadian federal holidays that create “long‑weekend” stretches** in 2023 (i.e., a holiday that falls on a weekday or is observed on a weekday, giving you at least three consecutive days off):

| Holiday | Date in 2023 | Observed (if shifted) | Long‑Weekend Span |
|---------|--------------|-----------------------|-------------------|
| New Year’s Day | Jan 1 (Sunday) | Observed Mon Jan 2 | Sat Dec 31 – Mon Jan 2 |
| Family Day (AB, BC, SK) | Feb 20 (Mon) | — | Sat Feb 18 – Mon Feb 20 |
| Family Day (ON) | Mar 13 (Mon) | — | Sat Mar 11 – Mon Mar 13 |
| Good Friday | Apr 7 (Fri) | — | Fri Apr 7 – Sun Apr 9 |
| Victoria Day | May 22 (Mon) | — | Sat May 20 – Mon May 22 |
| Canada Day | Jul 1 (Sat) | Observed Mon Jul 3 | Sat Jul 1 – Mon Jul 3 |
| Labour Day | Sep 4 (Mon) | — | Sat Sep 2 – Mon Sep 4 |
| Thanksgiving | Oct 9 (Mon) | — | Sat Oct 7 – Mon Oct 9 |
| Remembrance Day | Nov 11 (Thu) | Observed Mon Nov 13 | Thu Nov 11 – Mon Nov 13 |
| Christmas Day | Dec 25 (Mon) | — | Sat Dec 23 – Mon Dec 25 |

> **Quick notes**  
> • Some holidays (e.g., Family Day) vary by province, so the above table lists the dates for the provinces that observe them.  
> • Boxing Day (Dec 26) fell on a Tuesday in 2023, so it was observed on its actual day and did *not* create a long weekend.  

Feel free to plug these dates into your holiday‑planning app!
